advances: Extends exact finite physical cap, coarea and moment preservation to interior sources away from the maximum profile level.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Use the signed inverse-arm record formulas of 0586b032c888ffb0. Both arms are continuous, concave and nonincreasing, with positive values at level zero and a nonnegative sum throughout. Partition each arm $A$ separately at its internal zeros of $A(v)-sv$ and $A(v)+sv$ for every selected positive slope, and of $A(v)$ itself. Here and below the same reasoning applies to $B$. For any of these concave functions with positive value at zero, an interior zero determines its entire sign pattern. It is positive before that zero by the chord inequality with level zero, and negative afterward by the negative slope of that chord and concavity. If there is no internal zero the function is positive for $0\le v<R$ and nonnegative at $R$. This gives at most $2q+2$ cells per arm.

On a cell take the weight $w(v)=v^{m-2}$ if $m\ge2$, and $w=1$ if $m=1$. Add a constant to the whole arm on that cell large enough to make it nonnegative. Apply the local internal or terminal curvature-replacement lemma bb755603257fd80b to the shifted arm. The one-sided slopes needed there are finite at internal joins, since the original arm is finite and concave on their neighborhoods. At zero its right slope is bounded above by zero by nonincrease and below by a secant to any later level. The terminal lemma allows the final slope to be infinite. Subtract the same constant after the replacement. The first two recorded integrals are then still $\int wA$ and $\int vwA$. The quadratic record is still $\int wA^2$ by expanding the square and using preservation of the linear record. Curvature locations and slopes are unchanged by the shift.

The assembled arm keeps every internal partition value and its value at zero. At each join the new left derivative is at least the old left derivative, which is at least the old right derivative, which is at least the new right derivative. Thus it is continuous, concave and nonincreasing. Its final value can only rise. Each internal root in the partition therefore gives the same signs as before. If an expression had no internal root, its new endpoint values at zero and $R$ and its concavity keep it positive on $[0,R)$. In particular both arms have the same positivity boundaries as before on $[0,R)$, which preserves the maximum level whose superlevel interval contains the source $0$.

On each retained branch cell, the integrands for $V,P(s),C(s),M(s)$ in the signed record formulas are linear combinations of fixed functions of $v$ and $wA,vwA,wA^2$, separately for each arm. Indeed the outer branch of $j_s$ is a signed linear term with weight $v^{m-1}$, while the inner branch is a fixed term plus the quadratic term with weight $v^{m-2}$. The outer coarea term and the constant term of the inner moment are fixed on the branch, and the remaining terms are a linear and a quadratic term with weight $v^{m-2}$. For $m=1$ the terms with $m-1$ vanish and the only arm integral needed is $\int A$. At slope zero the preserved sign partition and weighted linear integral preserve $P(0)$. The preserved source height gives $C(0)=r(0)^m$, and $M(0)=0$. Thus all the finite records agree.

At the top, the two new arm values sum to at least their original nonnegative sum. At zero their sum is positive. Concavity makes it nonnegative on the full level interval. The set of $(z,v)$ with $0\le v\le R$ and $-\widehat B(v)\le z\le \widehat A(v)$ is a compact convex polygon with nested sections. Its upper boundary is the required concave piecewise affine profile, continuous also at both endpoints by compactness and the chord inequalities from the endpoints. The zero-level interval remains $[a,b]$ and the top section is nonempty. At most eight curvature locations per cell and at most one extra join per cell give the stated bound.

statement:
Let $m\ge1$ be an integer and let $r:[a,b]\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and concave with $a<0<b$ and $r(0)>0$. Put $R=\max r$ and write $\{z:r(z)\ge v\}=[-B(v),A(v)]$ for $0\le v\le R$. Use the planar measure of density $r(z)^{m-1}/2$ on $|x|\le r(z)$, $z\in[a,b]$. Write $V$ for its mass, $P(s)$ for the mass of $z+sx\ge0$, and $C(s),M(s)$ for the section integrals of the density and $z$ times the density on $z+sx=0$, with line measure divided by $\sqrt{1+s^2}$.

For any finite menu of $q$ positive slopes, with zero optionally included, there is a continuous concave piecewise affine profile on $[a,b]$ with the same $R$ and $r(0)$ and with the same $V$ and all selected $P(s),C(s),M(s)$ in its own physical density law. The replacement has at most $9(2q+2)$ curvature locations per inverse arm, including joins.
title: Finite-knot replacement preserves signed inverse-arm records
